title: Kansas ban on kratom, 7-OH takes effect July 1: help is available - NewsBreak
text:
1 days ago KANSAS (KOAM) - A Kansas ban on kratom and 7-hydroxymitragynine, also known as 7-OH, is set to take effect Wednesday, July 1, according to Community Health Center of Southeast Kansas.
The health center said some people who stop using kratom or 7-OH could experience withdrawal symptoms, including nausea, cold sweats, irritability, restlessness, physical pain, diarrhea, increased anxiety or depression, and mood swings.
CHC/SEK encouraged anyone experiencing medical or behavioral health concerns related to kratom or 7-OH to seek care without delay. The health center advised people to go to the nearest emergency room, walk-in clinic or a health care provider if they need immediate medical attention.
CHC/SEK said its medical providers can assess and treat withdrawal symptoms and connect patients with Addiction Treatment Services and Medication-Assisted Treatment, if appropriate. The organization also directed people to additional information and resources at dccca.org/kratom/ .
